stem.text: An open-top tray is made from a square sheet of tin 78 decimeters on a side by cutting a square of side x from each corner and folding up the sides. The tray can be at most 5 decimeters tall. Find the largest possible volume of the tray, in cubic decimeters.

worked_solution.text: The tray has height x and a square base of side \( 78 - 2 x \), so its volume is \( V(x) = x\left(78 - 2 x\right)^{2} \).
The cut must be positive, less than half the sheet, and at most 5, so the domain is \( 0 < x \le 5 \).
\( V'(x) = 12 \left(x - 39\right) \left(x - 13\right) \), which is zero at \( x = 13 \) and \( x = 39 \); only \( x = 13 \) lies strictly inside the sheet.
The critical point \( x = 13 \) is beyond the height limit, and \( V'(x) > 0 \) for every x in \( 0 < x \le 5 \), so V is increasing there and is largest at the right endpoint \( x = 5 \).
The largest volume is \( V(5) = 5\left(68\right)^{2} = 23120 \) cubic decimeters.

options.derivation: the shorter side of the base at the optimum reported instead of the volume
the height limit left out of the domain, so the critical point x = 13 is used
the side of the cut square, where the maximum occurs, reported instead of the volume
